name: cadre
description: Build a team of AI agents, wire them together with arrows, and watch them work.

enumDescriptions: Use the login your Claude Code CLI already has. Any ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in your shell is ignored.
Bill the Anthropic API per token. Set the key with “Cadre: Set API Key”.
cadre.billing.markdownDescription: How the team's work is paid for. The API key is never stored in settings — it lives in VS Code's encrypted secret storage.

enumDescriptions: Every edit and command needs your approval.
The team designs and reports but changes nothing.
No prompts at all. Secret files are still blocked.
cadre.autonomy.markdownDescription: How much rope the team gets. Enforced by the extension via a restrictive-only policy tier, so it holds even if your own Claude Code settings grant broader permissions.

cadre.inheritGlobalConfig.markdownDescription: Load your global `~/.claude/settings.json` as well as the project's. Off by default: blanket allow-rules that are reasonable for hand-driven Claude Code are not reasonable for an agent looping on its own. `CLAUDE.md` is loaded either way.

cadre.model.markdownDescription: Default model for agents that do not set their own. Use whatever your installed Claude Code offers — `default`, `opus`, `sonnet`, `haiku`, or a full id such as `claude-fable-5[1m]`. **Cadre: Settings → Default model** lists exactly what your CLI supports, including which models accept an effort level. Each agent can override this in the workflow builder.

cadre.effort.markdownDescription: Default reasoning depth. Empty lets each agent's capability preset decide.

cadre.maxDelegationDepth.markdownDescription: How many delegate arrows one chain of briefs may follow. A workflow may contain cycles — an agent asking back is a legitimate thing to draw — so this counter, not the shape of the graph, is what makes a run terminate. At the limit an agent keeps every other tool and simply loses its delegate tools.

cadre.maxContinuations.markdownDescription: How many times an agent may be continued after it runs out of turns. It is handed its own account of what it did and what it wrote, and carries on in the same lane — so a long job finishes instead of stopping halfway. Set to `0` to have a run simply stop and report. The context window is handled separately by Claude Code, which summarises the history and continues automatically.

cadre.playbooks.markdownDescription: Skills to load for the team (Claude Code Skills). Empty leaves the CLI's own defaults alone. Skills live in `.claude/skills/`.

cadre.connectors.markdownDescription:
MCP servers the team can reach, in the same shape as Claude Code's `mcpServers`. Give a teammate a connector and it appears in their tool list.

```json
{ "kaggle": { "type": "stdio", "command": "…" } }
```

cadre.claudeExecutablePath.markdownDescription: Absolute path to the `claude` executable. Empty auto-detects: bundled binary, then `PATH`, then the usual install locations.

enumDescriptions: Each teammate decides when and how much to reason. Recommended.
No extended thinking. Faster and cheaper; noticeably worse on hard problems.
cadre.thinking.markdownDescription: Extended thinking for the whole team. Reasoning streams into each lane under a collapsed **Reasoning** disclosure.

cadre.fallbackModel.markdownDescription: Model to fall back to when the primary is overloaded or a request is declined. The primary is retried at the start of each turn, so an outage does not permanently demote the session. Empty disables fallback.

cadre.maxSpendUsd.markdownDescription: Hard spend ceiling for a single run, in USD. The run stops when it is exceeded. `0` means no cap.

cadre.checkpoints.markdownDescription: Snapshot files before the team edits them, so **Cadre: Rewind Files** can restore the workspace to how it was at an earlier message.

cadre.additionalDirectories.markdownDescription: Absolute paths the team may read and edit in addition to the workspace folder.

cadre.plugins.markdownDescription: Local plugin directories. A plugin can ship commands, agents, skills and hooks.

cadre.exclusiveConnectors.markdownDescription: Use only the connectors in `cadre.connectors`, ignoring project `.mcp.json`, user settings and plugin-declared servers. Makes the team's tool surface fully predictable.

cadre.persistSessions.markdownDescription: Save conversations so they can be reopened with **Cadre: Resume Session**. Turn off for ephemeral work.

enumDescriptions: Document work that is substantial — the same threshold that creates a spec. A one-line fix gets nothing.
Document every change. Thorough, and noisy on small work.
No documentation duty. The team still reports to you in chat.
cadre.documentation.markdownDescription: Whether the team maintains documentation alongside the project. The Lead keeps `PROJECT.md`, the Researcher writes technical reports under `research/`, the Engineer keeps the changelog and code-level docs.

cadre.docsPath.markdownDescription: Workspace-relative folder for deliverable documentation. Unlike `.cadre/` (gitignored scratch), this is committed. The Lead and Researcher can write here directly; everything else still goes through the Engineer.

cadre.projectRoots.markdownDescription: Folders to scan for projects on the home screen. Empty scans beside the folders already open — e.g. with `~/Desktop/ai-team` open, it lists the projects in `~/Desktop`.

scripts.verify:all: npm run verify:fast && npm run verify:team

author: Muhammad Ahmed

virtualWorkspaces.description: Cadre runs the Claude Code CLI against files on disk.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: The team edits files and runs shell commands in the open folder.
